mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which typically precedes improved corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns. This relationship holds across all economic regimes without requiring additional conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between payroll growth and equity returns
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with positive PAYEMS change, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.2 percentage points within a single month signals monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through improved corporate revenue visibility and reduced recession risk.
evidence_refs: fact:Consumer spending accounts for 70% of GDP
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown regime defined by two consecutive months of declining industrial production (INDPRO), S&P 500 forward returns are negative due to reduced corporate output and earnings visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered manufacturing slowdown periods, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1300 thousand units signals strong residential construction activity, which typically precedes increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Residential construction contributes 15% to GDP growth
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with HOUST > 1300, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through improved corporate earnings and reduced recession risk.
evidence_refs: fact:Industrial production is a leading indicator of GDP growth
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with positive INDPRO change, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market regime defined by unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0%, S&P 500 forward returns are positive due to strong consumer spending and corporate hiring momentum.
evidence_refs: doc:Unemployment Rate and Stock Market Correlation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered tight labor market periods, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Annualized inflation exceeding 3.0% (computed from CPIAUCSL) signals persistent price pressures that prompt monetary tightening, predicting negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with annualized CPI > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.02.
